To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
net income is the most relevant performance measure, followed by operating cash flows, and then earnings before interest and taxes, while total sales is the least relevant performance measure.

the relative and incremental information contents of accounting-based performance variables in Egypt increase when moving down the income statement, and all of the accrually based performance measures have higher relative and incremental value relevancy compared with operating cash flows.
the relative and incremental values of accounting-based performance metrics in the Egyptian context are consistent with the results of prior research on developed countries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relative and incremental usefulness of a comprehensive set accounting-based measures of performance in the context of an emerging economy.
the value relevance of a broad set of financial performance measures in the emerging Egyptian capital market.
the value relevance of accounting performance measures in the emerging market of Egypt.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
accounting-based performance measures have value relevance in emerging markets.
the accrual-based metrics are more value-relevant in Egypt than the cash-based metrics.

the Egyptian capital market is not a perfect market and the investors do not fully understand the information provided by the accounting-based performance measures and therefore they do not fully use it in the decision making process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results highlight the importance and value relevance of accounting based metrics in Egypt.

accounting-based metrics have incremental and relative value-relevance for investors in the Egyptian capital market and this value-relevance is higher than the value-relevance of the operating cash flows.
the Egyptian capital market is still dominated by the bottom-line performance measure (net income) in the income statement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Egyptian capital market relies on accounting-based performance measures as the main source for assessing firms' performance.
the value-relevance of accounting-based performance metrics is not uniform across the income statement and the accrual-based metrics are more informative to the market than the operating cash flows.
accounting-based metrics are useful in emerging markets.
